newsitem.title: GERMANY: Oil World sees tight soyoil export supplies.
newsitem.headline: Oil World sees tight soyoil export supplies.

text.p: Export availability of soyoil should tighten from July as Latin American crushings slow down, the independent Oil World newsletter said on Tuesday.
High prices had encouraged Brazilian and Argentine farmers to market their crops quickly before the new U.S. harvest, which is due from September, it said.

Brazil would become an importer of probably one million tonnes of U.S. soybeans in the Oct/Jan 1997/98 period, when Argentina was also expected to import beans to meet oil and meal export commitments.
Brazil should also buy additional soyoil from abroad to satisfy domestic demand.
Low soybean stocks in South America in July and August would coincide with sharply increasing world vegetable oil demand, so consumers were also likely to draw on stocks.
Import demand for soyoil was currently strongest in China, North Africa, Iran, Pakistan and Bangladesh, while India was a potential buyer in June/July, depending on monsoon patterns.
Combined exports of soyoil from the U.S., Brazil and Argentina in March/May 1997 were pegged at 984,000 tonnes, compared with 771,000 in the same 1996 period.
